prompt: Write a clinical treatment summary (about 150 words) by the treating provider for a patient with wrist fracture after a low-speed head-on collision. The patient had 18 visits. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1405; do not mention it.)
text:
The patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with pain, swelling, and limited range of motion of the right wrist. Radiographs demonstrated a distal radius fracture with mild dorsal angulation and no intra-articular extension. Closed reduction was performed under local anesthesia, and the wrist was immobilized in a short-arm cast with post-reduction films confirming satisfactory alignment.

Over the course of 18 visits, the patient was monitored with serial radiographs to confirm maintenance of alignment and early callus formation. Cast immobilization continued for six weeks, followed by transition to a removable splint and a structured program of active and passive range-of-motion exercises, grip strengthening, and graded functional activities. Pain was managed with acetaminophen and short-term nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medication, and the patient reported steady improvement in function.

At the time of discharge from active care, the fracture had shown radiographic healing, the patient had regained most of the wrist flexion and extension, and grip strength was approaching the contralateral side. Residual stiffness and intermittent discomfort with heavy lifting are anticipated. Continued home exercise and periodic reassessment are recommended.
